title: Epochal prefetch coordinator for multi-GPU KV slicing and continuous batching
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement:
We need a coordinated, low-latency mechanism to prefetch and place KV cache slices across heterogeneous multi-GPU topologies so that continuous batching keeps tail latency low without blowing per-GPU memory budgets. Existing approaches either replicate hot keys (wasteful memory) or shard rigidly (high cross-GPU fetch latency and pipeline stalls).

Goal:
Design and implement an "epochal prefetch coordinator" that: (1) defines short-lived epochs aligned with continuous batching windows, (2) gathers per-epoch hot key access predictions, (3) issues coordinated prefetch/placement decisions across tensor- and pipeline-parallel boundaries, and (4) commits metadata in an async epoch commit so compute can proceed with minimal blocking. The coordinator should support: placement hints, speculative replication for hot prefixes, graceful fallback to remote fetch, and bounded memory accounting per GPU.

Key components and behavior:
- Epoch boundary: epochs are aligned to continuous-batcher flush windows (configurable, default 20ms). An epoch aggregates access frequencies and prefetch candidates for a short horizon.
- Local telemetry: each worker tracks per-request KV hits/misses and reports lightweight histograms to the coordinator at epoch end. Telemetry payloads are compact (bloom + top-k).
- Global decision: coordinator runs a fast placement heuristic (latency-weighted knapsack) that produces: local keep list, replica list, and a prefetch priority queue. Decisions are limited by per-GPU memory caps and by cross-GPU bandwidth budget for the epoch.
- Async epoch commit: placement actions are issued as non-blocking copy/prefetch ops with epoch IDs. Compute threads tag requests with epoch IDs; when a prefetch is late, request falls back to remote fetch path without blocking the compute pipeline.
- KV slice addressing: we introduce a compact epoched slice table (immutable per-epoch) that maps key ranges to owner/replica GPUs. Table updates are cheap (pointer swap) at epoch commit.
- Eviction policy: evict-by-epoch with grace TTLs to prevent oscillation. Hot keys get speculative replication for N epochs and then re-evaluated.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strong consistency vs availability: we choose eventual consistency per-epoch to avoid compute stalls. This sacrifices strict single-source-of-truth for slightly stale placement metadata, but avoids stalling pipeline parallel stages.
- Aggressive replication vs memory efficiency: replication helps tail latency but consumes memory. The heuristic uses cost models (token-frequency * latency-savings) to decide replication only when net benefit exceeds threshold. Threshold is tunable per-customer.
- Coordinator centralization: a single coordinator simplifies global decisions but could be a bottleneck. We design the coordinator to be sharded by model-slice range (hash) so decisions parallelize; fallback to local greedy heuristics if coordinator slow/unavailable.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Design proto: epoch metadata layout, telemetry schema, epoch table format (Confluence: https://company.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INFER/pages/EP-epochal-prefetch).
2) Coordinator service: lightweight C++ service living in runtime control plane with async RPC to workers. Start with single-process mode for canary.
3) Worker changes: sampling hooks in continuous-batcher to collect top-k hot keys per epoch; non-blocking prefetch API; per-epoch slice-table switch.
4) Placement heuristic: implement latency-weighted knapsack with bandwidth caps. Unit tests and synthetic microbenchmarks.
5) Rollout: canary on small models (gpt-medium) on Dedicated; metrics: 99.9th percentile latency, miss-rate, cross-GPU bandwidth. Global rollout gated on latency improvement and no memory regressions.

Metrics and observability:
- Per-epoch: hits/misses, prefetch-success-rate, replication cost (MB/epoch), bandwidth used, epoch decision time.
- Upstream: 99p/99.9p token latency, batch wait-time, memory pressure OOM counts.
- Dashboards: add per-model per-cluster views and alert if coordinator decision > 50ms or prefetch bandwidth > budget.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for placement heuristic and slice-table logic.
- Integration tests using multi-GPU local harness (3x A100 sim) to validate prefetch correctness and fallback behavior.
- Stress tests with adversarial access patterns (hot-key storms, zipf tail shifts) to measure oscillation and eviction behavior.

Architecture notes and alternatives evaluated:
- Bounded streaming prefetch vs epochal: epochal simplifies consistent placement across pipeline stages and aligns with batching windows; streaming prefetch had more complex rate control and oscillation.
- Centralized ML predictor: considered a learned predictor for hot keys; deferred because feature collection and retraining cost is high. The epochal heuristic is simpler and easier to tune.

Open decisions / questions:
- Default epoch window: 20ms vs 50ms. 20ms favored for low latency but increases decision churn.
- Replica TTL: number of epochs to keep speculative replicas (default 3).
- Coordinator sharding granularity: per-model-shard vs per-GPU-hash. We will prototype per-model-shard first.

Risks and mitigations:
- Slow coordinator: mitigated by sharding and local fallback greedy placement.
- Memory oscillation across epochs: mitigated by grace TTLs and hysteresis in eviction.
- Cross-GPU network spikes: budget with backpressure to prefetch queue and reject low-priority prefetches when network saturated.

Rollout plan and milestones:
- Week 0-1: finalize design doc and API (owner: Maya).
- Week 2-3: proto coordinator + worker sampling hooks behind runtime flag. Endpoint: canary with synthetic workload.
- Week 4: integration with continuous-batcher, unit/integration tests.
- Week 5-6: Dedicated canary on small model; collect metrics.
- Week 7: iterate heuristics and safety knobs; expand to medium models.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://company.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INFER/pages/EP-epochal-prefetch
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4218 (WIP)
- Benchmark harness: gs://redwood-bench/kv-epochal/2026-03-11

Acceptance criteria (for Done):
- Coordinator can make per-epoch placement decisions within 30ms median and 100ms p95 on our canary hardware.
- End-to-end 99.9p token latency improves or stays flat while memory headroom remains within configured caps.
- Eviction oscillation below threshold (measured as <2x per-key churn per minute under synthetic workloads).
